title: How much work is carrying a box?
hook: Carrying a heavy box across a room wears you out. How much work do your arms do on it?

knows: forces in newtons; a 10 kg mass weighs about 98 N
doesNotKnow: the physics definition of work, W = F d cos(theta)
that a force at right angles to the motion does no work

misconception: Holding or carrying a load along a level floor does work on it.
objective: The learner can explain that work is force times the distance moved along the force, so arms that only hold a box up do no work on it while it moves level, and do work only when it rises.

claims.text: In physics, work is force times the distance moved along the force's direction, measured in joules (J): W = F d cos(theta).
claims.source: OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 7.1 Work (W = F d cos theta; 1 J = 1 N m).

claims.text: Carried at a steady speed, a 10 kg box needs an upward push of 98.1 N from the arms and no sideways push.
claims.source: Constant velocity means zero net force (Newton's first law): the arms balance the weight m g = 10 x 9.81 = 98.1 N. Starting and stopping, which need a brief sideways push, are ignored and stated on stage ('steady speed').

claims.text: Carried 20 m along a level floor, the box rises 0 m, so the arms do 0 J of work on it.
claims.source: W = 98.1 N x 20 m x cos 90 deg = 98.1 x 0 m of rise = 0 J (node; work() in Demo.tsx).

claims.text: Carried 20 m up a 30° ramp the box rises 10 m (981 J of work); lifted 20 m straight up, 1962 J.
Your muscles still use energy to hold a load still or carry it level, though they do no work on the box.
claims.source: Muscle fibres consume ATP to maintain tension (isometric contraction) even with no external work; OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, section 10.3 Muscle Fiber Contraction and Relaxation; OpenStax University Physics Vol. 1, section 7.1 (holding a weight does no work on it).

recall.question: A waiter carries a tray at a steady speed across a level room, holding it up with 20 N. How much work does he do on the tray over 10 m?
recall.why: His push is straight up and the tray moves level, so it moves no distance along the push: no work is done on the tray.
